pancreas.context: The pancreas drawn as a long tapering gland with a wide head, a thin tail and its duct. Used in diabetes apps, digestive health content, endocrinology and anatomy lessons.

gallbladder.context: A pear-shaped gallbladder hanging from its duct with two gallstones inside. Used for gallstone and bile duct information, gastroenterology, surgery and anatomy content.

esophagus.context: A long food tube running down into the top of the stomach. Used for swallowing problems, heartburn and acid reflux information, gastroenterology and anatomy lessons.

trachea.context: The windpipe drawn as a ringed tube that divides into the two main bronchi. Used for airway, breathing and respiratory health content, ENT and anatomy lessons.

larynx.context: The voice box: a shield of cartilage with a notch on top sitting on the windpipe. Used for voice and throat health, speech therapy, ENT clinics and anatomy content.

vocal-cords.context: Vocal cords seen from above as two folds forming a V inside the throat opening. Used for voice care, singing lessons, speech therapy, laryngology and ENT content.

diaphragm.context: The dome-shaped diaphragm muscle arching beneath a pair of lungs. Used for breathing exercises, respiratory therapy, singing and yoga breath work, and anatomy lessons.

bronchial-tree.context: A windpipe branching again and again into smaller airways like an upside-down tree. Used for asthma, bronchitis and lung health content, pulmonology and anatomy lessons.

alveoli.context: A cluster of tiny round air sacs at the end of a small airway, like a bunch of grapes. Used for lung function, gas exchange, oxygen and respiratory medicine content.

heart-cross-section.context: The heart cut open to show four chambers divided by a central wall, with the great vessels on top. Used for cardiology, heart health education and anatomy lessons.

thymus.context: The two-lobed thymus gland drawn sitting just above a small heart. Used for immune system education, T cell and lymphatic topics, endocrinology and anatomy content.

bone-marrow.context: A long bone cut open lengthwise to show the spongy marrow inside. Used for bone marrow donation, stem cell transplant, blood cancer and hematology content.

adrenal-glands.context: A pair of kidneys, each topped by a small solid adrenal gland. Used for hormone and stress topics, endocrinology, adrenal disorders and anatomy lessons.

pituitary-gland.context: The brain in side view with the small pituitary gland hanging below it on a stalk. Used for hormone and growth topics, endocrinology, neurology and anatomy lessons.

prostate.context: The prostate gland wrapped around the tube that leads out of the bladder. Used for men's health, urology clinics, prostate cancer screening and anatomy content.

cochlea.context: The snail-shaped spiral of the inner ear with the hearing nerve leaving it. Used for hearing health, audiology, hearing loss and cochlear implant content.

eye-anatomy.context: Side cross-section of an eyeball with the lens at the front, the cornea bulge and the optic nerve at the back. Used for ophthalmology, optometry and vision health content.

brain-lobes.context: Side view of the brain divided by lines into its lobes, with the cerebellum below. Used for neuroscience lessons, neurology, psychology and brain function content.

cerebellum.context: Side view of the brain with the small striped cerebellum at the lower back drawn solid. Used for balance and coordination topics, neurology and neuroscience lessons.

brainstem.context: Side view of the brain with the stalk-like brainstem below it drawn solid. Used for neurology, vital functions such as breathing and heart rate, and neuroscience lessons.

brain-hemispheres.context: The brain seen from above, split down the middle into matching left and right halves with folds. Used for left brain and right brain topics, psychology, neurology and learning.

synapse.context: Two nerve endings facing each other across a small gap with chemical messengers crossing it. Used for neuroscience, neurotransmitter and brain chemistry topics, and psychology lessons.

spinal-cord.context: A long spinal cord with pairs of nerve roots branching out on both sides. Used for spinal injury and neurology content, back health, physiotherapy and anatomy lessons.

skin-layers.context: A block of skin in cross-section showing its layers, with a hair rising from the surface. Used for dermatology, skincare, cosmetics and biology lessons.

hair-follicle.context: A single hair growing out of its bulb-shaped follicle below the skin surface. Used for hair loss and hair growth content, trichology, dermatology and hair removal services.

tooth-anatomy.context: A molar cut in half showing the enamel crown, the pulp inside and two roots below the gum line. Used for dentistry, root canal treatment and dental education.

gums.context: A row of front teeth set into the bold scalloped band of the gums. Used for gum health, gum disease, periodontal care, dentistry and oral hygiene content.

incisor.context: A single front tooth with a flat biting edge and one long root, set at the gum line. Used for dental charts, dentistry, orthodontics and tooth care content.

canine-tooth.context: A single pointed canine tooth with a sharp tip and a long tapering root, set at the gum line. Used for dental charts, dentistry, orthodontics and tooth care content.

wisdom-tooth.context: An impacted wisdom tooth lying tilted under the gum line and pushing against the tooth next to it. Used for wisdom tooth removal, oral surgery and dental information.

dental-arch.context: A horseshoe-shaped row of teeth seen from above, divided into single teeth as on a dental chart. Used for dental records, orthodontics, dental clinics and bite planning.

respiratory-system.context: A head joined by the windpipe to a pair of lungs. Used for breathing and lung health content, respiratory medicine, pulmonology and biology lessons.

circulatory-system.context: A figure whose heart sends blood vessels out to the arms and legs. Used for circulation and heart health content, cardiology, blood flow topics and biology lessons.

femur.context: The femur: the long thigh bone with a ball-shaped head on an angled neck and two knobs at the knee end. Used for orthopedics, hip and leg injuries and anatomy lessons.

vertebra.context: A single vertebra seen from above with its round body, the ring for the spinal cord and three bony spurs. Used for spine health, chiropractic, orthopedics and anatomy lessons.

hand-skeleton.context: The bones of the hand: small wrist bones at the base with chains of finger bones spreading upward. Used for hand x-rays, orthopedics, hand surgery and anatomy lessons.

ball-and-socket-joint.context: A rounded bone head sitting in a cup-shaped socket, as in the hip or shoulder. Used for joint health, arthritis, orthopedics, joint replacement and physiotherapy content.

red-blood-cell.context: A red blood cell shown face on as a dimpled disc and edge on as a pinched oval. Used for blood tests, anemia, hematology, blood donation and biology lessons.

white-blood-cell.context: A white blood cell with a bumpy edge and a large lobed nucleus. Used for immune system topics, infections, blood tests, hematology and biology lessons.

sickle-cell.context: A crescent-shaped sickle red blood cell next to a normal round red blood cell. Used for sickle cell disease awareness, hematology, genetic conditions and blood health content.

antibody.context: A Y-shaped antibody molecule with two arms and a stem, drawn as a hollow outline. Used for immunity, vaccines, antibody tests, immunology and biology content.

chromosome.context: An X-shaped chromosome made of two banded arms pinched together at the centre. Used for genetics, DNA, heredity, genetic testing and biology lessons.

cell-division.context: A cell pinching in the middle into two new cells, each with its own nucleus. Used for mitosis and cell cycle lessons, growth and regeneration, and biology content.

mitochondrion.context: A capsule-shaped mitochondrion with its folded inner membrane running along its length. Used for cell biology lessons, energy and metabolism topics, and science content.

cancer-cell.context: An irregular lumpy cancer cell with an oversized nucleus and spiky edges. Used for oncology, cancer research, awareness and treatment content, and biology lessons.

stem-cell.context: A round stem cell with arrows leading to three smaller cells of different shapes. Used for stem cell research, regenerative medicine, cell therapy and biology lessons.

sperm-cell.context: A sperm cell with an oval head and a long wavy tail. Used for fertility clinics, male fertility and sperm tests, reproduction and biology lessons.

ovum.context: A large round egg cell with a thick outer layer, a nucleus and small cells ringing its edge. Used for fertility, ovulation, egg freezing, IVF and biology content.

fertilization.context: A sperm cell reaching the surface of a large egg cell, its tail trailing away. Used for conception, fertility treatment, IVF, pregnancy planning and biology lessons.

embryo.context: An early embryo drawn as a tight ball of cells inside a thin outer ring. Used for IVF and embryo transfer, fertility clinics, early pregnancy and embryology content.

fetus.context: A curled fetus inside the round womb, with a large head, tucked knees and the umbilical cord. Used for pregnancy apps, prenatal care, obstetrics and midwifery content.

rna.context: An RNA molecule drawn as a single wavy strand with base rungs sticking out on one side. Used for genetics, mRNA vaccines, molecular biology and science content.

bacteriophage.context: A bacteriophage virus shaped like a lunar lander, with an angular head, a straight tail and jointed legs. Used for microbiology, phage therapy and virus biology content.

spiral-bacteria.context: A corkscrew-shaped spiral bacterium with a thin whip tail at each end. Used for microbiology, infections such as Lyme disease and syphilis, and biology lessons.

streptococcus.context: A chain of small round bacteria linked in a gentle curve. Used for strep throat and bacterial infection content, microbiology, antibiotics and biology lessons.

glutes.context: Rear view of the hips and buttocks with the gluteal muscles highlighted. Used for glute workouts, leg day, fitness apps, physiotherapy and muscle anatomy content.

lats.context: Rear view of a torso with the wide latissimus muscles on each side of the back highlighted. Used for back workouts, pull-ups and rows, fitness apps and muscle anatomy content.

traps.context: Rear view of the neck and shoulders with the diamond-shaped trapezius muscle highlighted. Used for shoulder and upper back workouts, neck pain, fitness apps and physiotherapy.
